subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity modeling & GPU / TPS clarifications
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>

Subject: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity modeling & GPU / TPS clarifications

Hi Amelia —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we keep momentum. High-level asks from Fidelis: whether Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) is the right deployment mode vs Hosted API or Private VPC, and if Dedicated is preferred, a clearer sizing estimate (GPU class, TPS targets, concurrency assumptions, token mix) for procurement.

Recap of what we heard on the call:
- Primary workload: user-facing product search + personalization scoring (mix of short prompts and ticketed contextual prompts).
- Target SLO: p95 gen latency <= 250ms for autocomplete routes; background rerank <= 800ms.
- Expected steady TPS: 12 TPS average, with bursts to 90 TPS during peak marketing windows.
- Token mix: ~85% short requests (avg 60 tokens), 15% long context requests (avg 2,200 tokens) including retrieval context.
- Data requirements: customer data in VPC; but initial pilot could use Dedicated in our shared tenancy with strict isolation and SOC controls.

What I’m proposing:
1) We believe Dedicated capacity is the best path for predictable latency and cost for your mixed token profile. Hosted API may hit variability during bursts; Private VPC looks necessary later for full-data residency.
2) Attached is a first-pass sizing worksheet (fidelis-dedicated-sizing.csv) populated with the numbers above. We modeled two SKU families: A100-class (higher single-request latency but better throughput per card) and H100-class (lower latency / higher concurrency).
3) Immediate next steps:
   - Karthik to confirm kernel/concurrency assumptions for the 2,200-token tails and provide an ops playbook for burst handling.
   - Dylan to draft a pilot contract (1-month reserved pool + burst credits) and prepare an MSRP estimate for A100 vs H100 clusters.
   - Amelia to confirm whether Procurement prefers formal quote or SOW + PO route.

Attachments: fidelis-dedicated-sizing.csv, redwood-deploy-options.pdf

Action: Can you confirm these numbers by EOD Wed so we can lock a pilot quote? Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up with Karthik and Dylan if you want a walk-through of the worksheet.

Thanks,

—Diego Fernandez

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Dedicated capacity modeling & GPU / TPS clarifications

Diego —

Thanks for the summary. Quick technical notes after skimming the worksheet:

- Token mix and long-tail behavior matter: the 2,200-token context requests will dominate memory and KV-cache pressure. For those, we should assume a lower effective concurrency (approx 4-6 concurrent long requests per H100) due to KV thrash.
- For the 85% short requests (~60 tokens) we can bank on high packing and continuous batching; an H100 can sustain ~250 short-TPS equivalent under efficient batching, A100 nearer 160 (estimates include quantization profile we discussed).
- Recommendation: pilot with a small H100 pool (2 x H100) + autoscale policy for burst to additional H100s or fallback to a slightly cheaper A100 pool for background rerank jobs. This gives the best balance for your p95 250ms target.
- Burst strategy: implement a policy that routes short critical routes to the H100 pool and less-critical/background reranks to the A100 fallback pool. We should set a throttling guard at 120% of steady TPS to avoid cold autoscale storms.

I’ll update the worksheet with per-card TPS assumptions and an ops note about KV-cache sizing. Also adding expected memory-per-session for long contexts so Diego can include in the pricing.

Karthik
Principal Infra / Serving
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick recap and for the worksheet. A few clarifications from our side after internal sync:

- The long-context requests (2,200 tokens) are primarily admin/agent escalation flows and will be ~10–15% of production (we had conservatively estimated 15% on the call).
- Procurement: we prefer a formal quote + PO route for pilots if pricing is fixed for the month. PO is easier for our AP team.
- For the pilot we can commit to the 1-month reserved pool and want a clear overspend cap (we can absorb 25% burst beyond committed TPS).

Can you provide:
- A short one-pager with the proposed pilot configuration (GPU class, node count, burst policy, estimated monthly cost range).
- One-line description of fallback behavior (how we degrade to A100, or routing to Hosted if we hit capacity).

If you can get that to procurement and me by Wednesday EOD we’ll aim to sign and issue a PO the following week. We’re generally aligned with Karthik’s recommendations.
